inputs.original_text: This isn’t reassurance—it’s a pressure tactic. Tom Homan refusing to rule out enforcement at polling places, then asking what Democrats are “afraid of,” helps plant doubt about whether voting is safe while giving the administration room to deny it meant to intimidate anyone. The conflicting answers look less like confusion than a way to keep the threat alive without taking responsibility for it.
inputs.modified_text: This looks like a deliberately calibrated strategy: Tom Homan keeps enforcement at polling places on the table, then frames Democrats as “afraid of” something, while the administration preserves room to deny any intent to intimidate. The mixed signals aren’t a harmless muddle—they keep voters uncertain and the threat usable, while responsibility stays conveniently blurred.
